Devon —

Great to hear, and thanks for the clear asks. Short answers up front: yes to both, with a couple of implementation details. I've attached an entitlement matrix draft that maps the typical reseller trial/paid/co-sell buckets to Redwood SKU and marketplace metering attributes.

Key notes: 
1) Reseller trial SKU: we can create a time-limited trial SKU in the marketplace catalog that bills to your reseller account but carries an attribution tag for co-sell reporting. That tag is what triggers revenue attribution in the co-sell telemetry.

2) Demo tenant: we can provision a sandbox tenant with separate metering so run-rate tokens are simulated against a sandbox billing profile. That keeps production telemetry clean. The demo tenant can be configured to auto-reset every 30 days and we can expose a short API endpoint for tenant resets.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben, can you validate the config below and add any technical constraints?
- Laura, can you confirm whether we need a DocuSign SOW or if a mutual action plan (MAP) is sufficient for provisioning access pre-listing?

I'll schedule a 30-minute call for Wednesday to walk the Maya engineering and revops teams through the entitlement matrix and tenant provisioning flow.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Partner Solutions | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Connor / Devon —

Quick technical notes inline: 

> Reseller trial SKU: we can create a time-limited trial SKU in the marketplace catalog that bills to your reseller account but carries an attribution tag for co-sell reporting.

This is correct. Implementation details: the marketplace SKU will have a metadata field (co_sell_tag) that we set to "maya_co_sell_v1". Marketplace metering pushes a webhook to our billing pipeline; we will add an attribute to the event so HubSpot/HB-3456721 can read attribution for reporting.

> Demo tenant: we can provision a sandbox tenant with separate metering so run-rate tokens are simulated against a sandbox billing profile.

We will spin up a tenant in the Redwood sandbox namespace with a simulated billing adapter. Limitations: exports from sandbox will be aggregated separately and cannot be used for production reconciliation. If Maya needs deterministic invoice-able usage for a demo (rare), we can provision a dedicated trial account instead (requires a short SOW).

I attached a short tenant provisioning checklist and a script snippet to reset usage counters. Also added a short note on permission scopes for reseller reps so they can see aggregated usage but not customer PII.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
